summary: try/except lets your program handle an error and keep running. raise reports an error from your own code when a value breaks the rules.
notes: except ValueError as error stores the error so you can print its message.
else runs only if the try block succeeded. finally runs every time.
raise ValueError(...) sends the error to the caller's except block.
pitfall: A bare except: with no type catches every error, including typos like NameError, which hides bugs. Name the error type you expect.
